introSlide.heading: 5 things most people get wrong about Taiwan's Gold Card
introSlide.description: 4-in-1 document, tax exemption, PR path. But not how you think.

slides.heading: ❌ Gold Card = just a work visa
slides.description: It's 4-in-1: work permit + visa + ARC + re-entry. One document.

slides.heading: ❌ Spouse gets automatic work rights
slides.description: Separate MOL application required. Not automatic.

slides.heading: ❌ High earners get PR in 1 year
slides.description: 3 years continuous residence. HK/Macau exception only.

slides.heading: ❌ Tax break covers all income
slides.description: 50% exemption on salary ABOVE NT$3M only. First 5 years.

slides.heading: ❌ Pension starts on day 1
slides.description: Tied to APRC status, not Gold Card employment.

endingSlide.heading: Which one surprised you?

caption:
Taiwan's Gold Card sounds simple until you actually read the fine print.

Most people assume it's just a work visa, that their spouse can work automatically, or that the tax break cuts their whole salary in half. None of those are true.

The Gold Card is a 4-in-1 document (work permit + visa + ARC + re-entry), the tax exemption only applies to salary above NT$3M, and your spouse still needs a separate MOL application. PR takes 3 years, not 1.

Still one of Asia's best remote-work pathways. Just know what you're signing up for.

Which myth caught you off guard? Drop it in the comments.
